newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo denies in talks on Southern stake.
newsitem.headline: Anglo denies in talks on Southern stake.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South African Ltd said on Wednesday that it had no intention to sell its stake in insurer Southern Life.
Business Day newspaper said earlier that Worldwide Africa Investments was in discussion with Anglo on a sale and was mulling a joint bid with black investment group Kopano Ke Matla.
But Anglo director and Southern deputy chairman Mike King told Reuters that the firm did not plan to sell its interest.
"We are not in negotiations and we have no intention to sell," he said.
King said that he had received a number of phone calls from interested parties following market speculation on Anglo selling its slices of Southern and First National Bank.
"Many people have phoned concerning any plans we might have about First National and Southern... but I don't take a phone call as meaning having negotiations with someone," he said.

There has been speculation on bringing a black group into Southern Life following the successes in capturing black customers by rival insurer Metropolitan Life, controlled by black group New Africa Investments Ltd.
King said the idea had its attractions, but stressed there were no current plans to do so.
Anglo has recently sold major stakes in Johnnic and JCI to black empowerment groups and King said the firm was happy that its restructuring had gone far enough so far.
"We feel we have done our bit in bringing black groups into JCI and Johnnic," he said.
